cases.claim_in_row: the row's own Departure text admits 'B and Mg are non-magnetic impurities ... negligible magnetic susceptibility', then pivots the magnetic-gradient mechanism to 'separate ferrous tramp (which might be co-mingled)'
cases.verification: dissolved ions' volume susceptibility (diamagnetic/paramagnetic, x ~ 1e-6 class) gives magnetic body forces orders of magnitude below thermal (kT) mixing at any practical B.gradB; and ferrous-tramp removal does not address the STATED failure mode (B/Mg chemical degradation of battery-grade lithium) — the mechanism neither acts on the target species nor survives the row's own admission
cases.verdict: CONFIRMED — mechanism dodges the stated problem (off-target pivot inside the answer)

cases.claim_in_row: 'cathodic_protection_sizing through a sacrificial anode array directly coupled to the anode bus'
cases.verification: cathodic protection drives the protected metal to be the CATHODE against a sacrificial anode; the anode bus in an electrolytic cell is at ANODIC (positive) potential — coupling a sacrificial array to it puts both at anodic polarity (the 'protected' member stays the anode; the array just corrodes additionally), and the anode's deliberate dissolution IS its electrode function — protecting it cathodically defeats the cell
cases.verdict: CONFIRMED — polarity inversion, provable from the galvanic-series definition

cases.error_class: MAGNITUDE (decidable by arithmetic, not an assumption dispute)
cases.claim_in_row: 'the total neutralizable acid load is 2 kg/h; injecting 100 L/h of 10% slurry releases ~142 kJ of heat' offered as a duct-wall thermal effect
cases.verification: pint recompute: 10,000 m3/h x 200 ppm SO2 = 89.2 mol/h = 5.72 kg/h SO2 (their 2 kg/h is ~3x low); neutralization at their own 57.3 kJ/mol -> 5113 kJ/h = 1420 W (their ~142 kJ is ~36x low); over ~100 m2 of duct wall that is 14.2 W/m2 -> wall dT ~ 1.4 K against 10 W/m2K convection — no stated corrosion-prevention thermal effect is reachable; the heat is 2-3 orders too small for the claimed purpose
cases.verdict: CONFIRMED — magnitude error 36x on the energy number and the effect ~2 orders below physical significance

cases.claim_in_row: 'By adding mass to the main journals (increasing inertia) ... we shift the natural frequency f_n = (1/2pi)sqrt(k/I) above the maximum firing frequency', conceding mid-passage 'Increasing I_eff by 50% reduces f_n by sqrt(1.5) (i.e., lowers it) or ... we increase stiffness k_eff'
cases.verification: f_n = (1/2pi)sqrt(k/I): dI>0 strictly LOWERS f_n (their own 1.22 arithmetic concedes it); raising f_n requires a stiffness increase, and the row's described modification (added journal mass) contains NO stiffness mechanism — the lead mechanism contradicts its own governing relation and the rescue path is not in the design
cases.verdict: CONFIRMED — wrong-signed lead claim; the honest mechanism (stiffening) is asserted without a physical implementation

cases.claim_in_row: 'permittivity eps_i = 5.0 F/m'; uniform-gap formula 'E_max = V ln(r_o/r_i) / (r_i (r_o - r_i))' evaluated as '320000 x ln(4)/(0.02 x 0.06) ~ 37 kV/mm'; graded claim 'E_max reduces to ~15-18 kV/mm'
cases.verification: pint: their formula's DIMENSIONS are V/m^2, not V/m — a field formula with the wrong dimensions is invalid as written (the pint DimensionalityError is the exhibit); the correct coaxial solution E_max = V/(r_i ln(r_o/r_i)) = 14.6 kV/mm (their printed 37 kV/mm is ~2.5x the correct value AND inconsistent with their own inputs r_i=0.02, r_o=0.06 where they typed (r_i x r_o) as the denominator pair); '5.0 F/m' as absolute permittivity implies eps_r ~ 5.6e11 — the intended value is the dimensionless eps_r=5.0 (absolute ~4.4e-11 F/m): the unit label breaks every downstream field relation
cases.verdict: CONFIRMED — dimensionally invalid formula + absolute/relative permittivity unit mislabel

cases.claim_in_row: 'local field reduction factor R = eps_ins / eps_eff = 3.5 / 1.8 = 1.94' for a low-permittivity porous pad (eps_r ~ 1.1-1.3) inserted at the barrier interface to 'locally reduce the electric field intensity'
cases.verification: D-continuity for series dielectrics (normal field): E_low-eps/E_ins = eps_ins/eps_layer — the LOW-permittivity layer sees a HIGHER field, and the adjacent defect site in the high-eps insulation sees the field INCREASE by ~1.94x, not decrease; stress grading works by RAISING local permittivity (high-k fillers) or graded conductivity, never by inserting voids in series; the claimed reduction is the reversed relation
cases.verdict: CONFIRMED — wrong-signed relation (the owner's exemplar of the re-labeling prohibition)
